synthesis.headline: 72 scheme entries cover the global retail/wholesale/cross-border rail map well (the Big-Four card networks, every major real-time rail — UPI, Pix, FedNow, RTP, SCT Inst, FPS, PIX-class A2A — plus RTGS, ACH-batch, wallets, and cross-border infra SWIFT/CLS/CIPS/PAPSS), but the catalog has 6 duplicate ids (visa, mastercard, unionpay, american-express, discover/diners-discover, rupay each appear twice as network + global-acceptance variants) that must be de-duped before any enum or KB wiring. Source quality is uneven and self-labeled: trust the `authoritative` entries (most public-operator rails: Payments Canada, Fed, Nacha, ECB/Eurosystem, Pay.UK, NPCI, BCB Pix, ABS/AusPayNet) and treat the `weak`/`mixed` ones (notably the Visa/Mastercard/UnionPay brand entries and several APAC/MEA operators) as needing a sourced KB doc before they ship. Logo guidance is sound and matches the app's existing brands.ts posture: only ~9 schemes have genuine CC0 simple-icons marks; everything else is official-mark-with-trademark-caveat or styled wordmark chip — do not fabricate logo artwork for the ~50 rails without a CC0 mark.

Fed, ECB/Eurosystem, Bank of England, Banco de Mexico, RBI, BCB, PBoC — operators of RTGS (Fedwire, T2, CHAPS, Lynx) and instant rails (FedNow, Pix). A distinct civic-building glyph separates the monetary authority from commercial banks.

Card networks (Visa/Mastercard/UnionPay/RuPay) and A2A scheme operators (Interac, NPCI-UPI, Pay.UK, NPP) that route auth/clearing. Network node glyph denotes the hub that switches between issuer and acquirer.

The technical intermediary (BaaS processor, payment gateway, acquiring processor) that formats ISO 8583/20022 and connects merchant to network; 'intermediary' node type. Chip glyph signals message-processing infrastructure.
Batch/netting operators — FedACH, EPN, ACSS, STEP2-T, EBA CLEARING, Bacs. Layered glyph evokes batched, netted settlement distinct from a real-time switch.
Alipay, WeChat Pay, M-Pesa, CoDi — stored-value or pass-through wallets that sit between consumer and bank rail. Wallet glyph is unambiguous and matches the schema's wallet rail type.

The non-bank program manager riding a sponsor bank (the FoF Studio core scenario — FBO/sponsor-bank flows). Needs to be visually distinct from the chartered 'institution' it rides on; a non-building glyph signals 'not the issuer of record'.
The USD/EUR correspondent sitting between originating and beneficiary banks on cross-border legs. A directional-exchange glyph distinguishes the pass-through correspondent role from a terminal bank.

Currency conversion and CLSSettlement payment-versus-payment for cross-currency flows (CAD->USD and beyond). A two-currency exchange glyph marks where FX rate/spread and PvP settlement occur — separate from money movement.
SWIFT, CIPS, PAPSS — the international rails/messaging layers. A globe denotes the cross-border tier; pairs with the rule that SWIFT carries messages, not money.
OSFI, OCC, FDIC, CFPB, FCA, RBI, SAMA, FINTRAC — oversight bodies surfaced in the compliance/regulatory lenses. Scales of justice glyph denotes supervision/rules rather than money flow.
The pooled For-Benefit-Of or settlement account where program funds actually sit (central to sponsor-bank accuracy). A vault glyph marks a balance-holding account distinct from an institution party.

recommendations: De-dup and normalize the catalog FIRST: collapse the 6 duplicate ids (visa, mastercard, unionpay, american-express, discover/diners-discover, rupay each appear twice), reconcile RuPay's two hexes (#097939 vs #097D40), and fix the SADAD brandColorHex which contains a Cyrillic 'А' (U+0410) and won't parse as hex. A diagram that ships with a malformed color or a double-rendered Visa node breaks the accuracy thesis before any rail logic runs.

Do NOT widen the schema enums yet. Keep JurisdictionSchema=['CA','US'] and CurrencySchema=['CAD','USD'] as the hard accuracy lock. Add new jurisdictions/currencies one region at a time, and only in lockstep with a sourced KB doc + a passing seed — never open the enum to all 72 schemes at once. Region rollout order by source strength and importance: (1) EU/SEPA + Eurosystem (EUR), (2) UK/Pay.UK + CHAPS (GBP), (3) Mexico/SPEI (MXN, completes North America), (4) Brazil/Pix and India/UPI (BRL/INR, both authoritative + CC0-or-clean wordmark), then APAC/MEA last where source authority is mostly 'mixed'.

Gate every scheme behind a KbDoc in knowledge.ts with verified operator/regulator sources[] — the same contract the CA/US docs already use. A scheme that has no KB doc must remain ungenerable, not silently rendered. Prioritize authoring docs for the 'authoritative' entries; explicitly hold the 'weak'/'mixed' entries (the Visa/Mastercard brand rows, CIPS, CNAPS, several APAC operators) until their KB doc cites a primary source. This keeps the Sources panel honest as coverage grows.

Preserve the composer's honest-refusal + adapted-caveat as the global-coverage safety net. The existing logic (low-confidence refusal, <2-signal adapted flag, and the CA/US jurisdiction guard) is exactly the right shape — extend the jurisdiction guard so that ANY prompt naming a region without a shipped KB doc gets an adapted caveat or refusal, never a confident diagram. A polished wrong global flow is more damaging than a CA/US refusal because the user has less ability to catch the error.

Extend brands.ts incrementally with the verified CC0 marks only: add siUnionpay, siJcb, siAlipay, siWechat, siPix, siSwift to the BRANDS table (Visa/MC/Amex/Discover already present). For every other rail, add a styled wordmark chip with the catalog's brand hex — never fabricate logo artwork. Carry the trademarkNote text into a title/aria attribute so 'identification use only' travels with the mark into exhibit PNG exports.

Model the new institution types as schema subtypes, not new node 'type' enum values. The node 'type' enum (endpoint/institution/intermediary/treasury) is intentionally small; map central bank, scheme operator, clearing house, correspondent, FX/CLS, wallet, fintech/program-manager, and regulator onto the free-form 'subtype' field plus the lucide icon mapping above. This adds global expressiveness without loosening the structural contract that keeps validation tight.

Encode two rail-class invariants before going global, because both have already shipped as P0 bugs: (a) messaging networks (SWIFT, and arguably CIPS messaging) must never carry a MONEY edge — they ride notification/messaging legs only; (b) settlement infra (CLS, RTGS operators) and card networks must net/settle, not move retail money directly. Add these as KB facts and composer guards so the first non-CA/US generations don't repeat the wire-fx SWIFT-carrying-money error at global scale.

Flag emerging/non-traditional rails (stablecoin on/off-ramps, and sanctions-affected Mir) with an explicit on-canvas disclosure rather than a clean rail chip. The catalog already marks these out-of-traditional-rails / sanctions-affected; surface that as a warning annotation (the schema's annotation type='warning' already exists) so a generated flow never implies frictionless global acceptance that doesn't exist.
